parts.note: the French word for 'of' is de
a fiancé is a betrothed lover

explanation.surface: Someone asks how belligerent France's lover is.
explanation.walkthrough: The charade runs in answer order: the French 'of' comes first, then the betrothed lover.
explanation.definitionFit: Defiance is a bold, challenging attitude, a form of aggressiveness toward authority.

clue.text: What Buridan's ass couldn't make, to save its life!

definitions.text: What Buridan's ass couldn't make, to save its life!

parts.words: What Buridan's ass couldn't make, to save its life!
parts.note: in the philosophers' fable, Buridan's ass starved between two equal haystacks, unable to choose either

explanation.surface: A nod to the old fable of a donkey dying from indecision.
explanation.definitionFit: The ass starved because it could not choose, so what it failed to make was a choice.

clue.text: Right, old boy — enter the Admiral as an English sailor

indicators.note: the first two pieces go into the admiral's name, as if entering it

parts.note: Admiral Jacky Fisher, First Sea Lord in the early 1900s
OB is the abbreviation for old boy, a former pupil

explanation.surface: An old schoolboy is signed on to serve under the admiral.
explanation.walkthrough: R and OB are put inside FISHER. Martin Frobisher was an Elizabethan English seaman and explorer.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Martin Frobisher was an Elizabethan navigator, an English mariner who sought the Northwest Passage.

clue.text: Advantage the short girl gives up

indicators.note: in a down clue, giving something up raises it, so the name is read from bottom to top

parts.note: Tessa is a short form of the girl's name Theresa

explanation.surface: A small girl concedes a lead in some game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gives up' turns TESSA so that it reads upward in the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: An asset is something useful or valuable, a benefit that puts you ahead.

parts.note: choler is an old word for anger, from the bile thought to cause it

explanation.surface: Someone flares up just as they fall ill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shows' and 'getting' are links: anger plus A displays the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Cholera is an acute bacterial infection of the intestine, an often fatal illness.

parts.note: she is the pronoun for a woman

indicators.note: a maker shapes material, so the letters of hat are reshaped

explanation.surface: A milliner who is female, in this particular instance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'maker' rearranges HAT into EATH, after SHE.
explanation.definitionFit: A sheath is a close-fitting cover, the case for a knife or sword blade.

parts.note: hops are the cone-like fruit of the hop plant, used in brewing
Scotch is whisky

explanation.surface: Someone has fruit and a whisky once the match is over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' is a link here: the pieces come before the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Hopscotch is a children's playground pastime of hopping through chalked squares.

indicators.note: the answer lies within the words lama's sanctuary, running across the word gap

explanation.surface: A Tibetan monk hoards things in his temple.
explanation.definitionFit: To amass is to gather together a large quantity, to pile up.

parts.note: to hone a blade is to sharpen it

indicators.note: the opening letter of tin is taken, as if the word were opened

explanation.surface: A gadget that only puts an edge on a can-opener.
explanation.walkthrough: 'opener' gives T, the first letter of 'tin', after HONES.
explanation.definitionFit: A just person is fair and upright, truthful in dealings.

parts.note: the Church season of the coming of Christ spans the four weeks before Christmas

explanation.surface: A forecast that something is due soon.
explanation.walkthrough: The word means an arrival, and the Church season it names lasts about four weeks.
explanation.definitionFit: The season before Christmas marks the arrival of Christ and lasts roughly a month.

clue.text: But this kind will not disqualify you for the Dunmow flitch

definitions.text: But this kind will not disqualify you for the Dunmow flitch

parts.words: But this kind will not disqualify you for the Dunmow flitch
parts.note: the flitch of bacon at Dunmow in Essex goes to couples who have not had an angry exchange for a year; this puzzle is no bar

explanation.surface: A remark about the old Essex prize for marital harmony.
explanation.walkthrough: The Dunmow Flitch is an English custom awarding bacon to married couples who have not quarrelled for a year and a day; an angry word would disqualify them, a puzzle would not.
explanation.definitionFit: Read as two words, a peevish remark; read as one, the puzzle the solver is doing.

definitions.meaning: flat and level, as in a smooth expanse
unattractive, a polite word for homely looks

explanation.surface: A level surface that looks unattractive.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is level or unbroken ground; the other is homely in appearance.

definitions.meaning: to be sparing, to hold back in supply
a small sandpiper of shores and mudflats

explanation.surface: A plea to spare the bird's life.
explanation.definitionFit: To stint is to skimp or ration; the word also names a small wading sandpiper.

indicators.note: in its old sense of outside, the cutting word goes round the hesitation

parts.note: to excise is to cut out
er is the sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: Without pausing, someone cancels some rail services.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' means outside here, so EXCISES goes round ER. 'trains' is a verb, not railway carriages.
explanation.definitionFit: To train is to drill or practise, as a coach works through drills.

parts.note: in Hamlet, Gertrude tells how an envious sliver of willow broke and the girl fell into the brook and drowned

explanation.surface: A line about someone hurt by a spiteful splinter.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase quotes Gertrude's report in Shakespeare's Hamlet: 'an envious sliver broke' and Polonius's daughter drowned.
explanation.definitionFit: Hamlet's beloved drowned when a willow branch snapped beneath her.

definitions.meaning: bringing someone into a secret or scheme

explanation.surface: Confessing that one has been drawn into something.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis joins this clue to the next, where the same idea moves to golf.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means allowing entry, and also letting someone in on a plan.

clue.text: Irritable and so on in your old surroundings

indicators.note: the abbreviation for and so on sits inside the old word for your
the archaic possessive forms the surroundings that enclose the middle piece

parts.note: thy is the archaic form of your
etc is the abbreviation of et cetera

explanation.surface: Grumpy and the like when back in familiar haunts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in your old surroundings' puts ETC inside THY.
explanation.definitionFit: Tetchy describes someone touchy and bad-tempered, quick to take offence.

parts.note: a golfer's correct putt sends the ball into the cup, finishing the hole

explanation.surface: Following on from the previous clue: fixing a problem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'putting' is golf's putting, not placing: a correct putt finishes the hole.
explanation.definitionFit: In golf the phrase means sinking the ball with the final stroke on a green.

clue.text: Likes to set out in my foreign fur

indicators.note: the rearranged letters sit within the French word for my

parts.note: mon is French for my

indicators.note: setting out the letters arranges them anew

explanation.surface: Someone likes to set off wearing a fur from abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to set out' rearranges LIKES into LESKI, which goes inside MON.
explanation.definitionFit: Moleskin is the pelt of the mole, a soft short pile.

clue.text: They may hold up coal supplies

definitions.text: They may hold up coal supplies

parts.words: They may hold up coal supplies
parts.note: fireplace bars support the fuel burning on a hearth

explanation.surface: A complaint about something delaying fuel deliveries.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hold up' reads as delay, but means support: the iron frames hold burning coal.
explanation.definitionFit: These iron frames in a fireplace hold the burning fuel.

clue.text: Tried to find the class talking

indicators.note: speaking a word turns it to sound, so its pronunciation counts

parts.note: a sort is a class or kind

explanation.surface: Someone looked for the class while chatting.
explanation.walkthrough: In a non-rhotic British accent SORT and SOUGHT sound the same.
explanation.definitionFit: Sought is the past tense of seek, meaning searched for.

parts.note: OT is the Old Testament, part of the Bible
hello is a greeting

explanation.surface: A North African says hello in scriptural style.
explanation.walkthrough: Shakespeare's Moor of Venice is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's tragic hero is the Moor of Venice.

clue.text: Drink too much and go over the edge ?

parts.note: over means excessively, as in overdo
to lap is to drink like a cat

explanation.surface: Someone drinks to excess and loses control.
explanation.walkthrough: 'go over the edge' sounds like losing control; here it means extending past a margin.
explanation.definitionFit: To overlap is to extend past a border and cover part of something else.

definitions.meaning: in cricket, a batsman who plays on deflects the ball onto his own stumps and is out
to keep going, continue the game

explanation.surface: Contradictory orders: leave and stay.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, playing on means edging the ball onto your own wicket, so you are out.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket the phrase means being bowled off one's own bat; generally it means continuing.

clue.text: Languor of girl-something due to upset

parts.note: lass is a girl
it stands for an unnamed thing

indicators.note: upsetting the letters knocks them into a new order

explanation.surface: A young woman's lethargy is down to some upset.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to upset' rearranges DUE into UDE.
explanation.definitionFit: Lassitude is weariness and lack of energy, a languid state.

parts.note: a bob was a shilling, abbreviated s
Leigh Hunt was an English Romantic poet and essayist

explanation.surface: Sidetrack a man called Bob Leigh.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bob' and 'Leigh' look like one person's name. A bob is slang for a shilling, an old British coin, written s; Leigh Hunt was a 19th-century poet.
explanation.definitionFit: To shunt is to move aside or divert, as railway wagons onto a siding.

parts.note: a sin is an offence against moral law
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: After sinning, someone goes to church.
explanation.definitionFit: Since can mean from a past time onward, that is, subsequently.

definitions.meaning: an old pointed writing tool, a stylus

explanation.surface: A question about a typewriter.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means a sort or manner, and also an old pointed instrument for writing.

definitions.meaning: Brigham ... was the Mormon leader who founded Salt Lake City

explanation.surface: Asking about a Mormon's children.
explanation.walkthrough: Brigham Young led the Mormons to Utah.
explanation.definitionFit: Brigham Young led the Mormon church; the word also means an animal's brood.

parts.note: holly is an evergreen tree
hock is a German white wine

explanation.surface: A gardener plants a tree and fetches some wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plant' is the definition, a noun, not the verb it seems.
explanation.definitionFit: The hollyhock is a tall flowering garden plant of the mallow family.

parts.note: someone out is not in
G is a string on a violin or guitar

explanation.surface: Measuring out lines with a piece of string.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' gives NOT IN and 'string' gives G, a violin string.
explanation.definitionFit: Noting means observing and recording, taking note of.

clue.text: Sole connection with a number of the top people

parts.note: a shoe's upper is the part attached to the sole
ten is a number

explanation.surface: A link with some of the elite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sole' is the bottom of a shoe, not 'only': the upper joins it.
explanation.definitionFit: The upper ten (thousand) is an old phrase for the aristocracy, the social elite.
